items.title: Pay operating cost balance (Nachzahlung)
items.quote: Wir bitten um Zahlung der Nachforderung bis zum 08.01.2027.
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date for the payment: 08.01.2027. This date is set directly by the landlord in the letter, so it is taken as given rather than computed from a period. (For reference: 2027-01-08 is a Friday, a normal business day, so no weekend/holiday shift applies.)

items.title: Raise objections (Einwendungen) to the Betriebskostenabrechnung
items.quote: Einwendungen gegen diese Abrechnung teilen Sie uns bitte schriftlich mit.
items.computation: The letter itself names no deadline for objections, only asking that they be communicated in writing. German tenancy law (§ 556 Abs. 3 S. 5 BGB) gives the tenant 12 months after receipt of the statement to raise objections (unless the tenant was not responsible for missing this period). The statement was handed over by messenger directly into the letterbox on 18 November 2026 at 11:05, so receipt = 2026-11-18. Counting under § 187 Abs. 1 BGB starts the next day; the 12-month period under § 188 Abs. 2 BGB ends on 2027-11-18 (a Thursday), which is a normal working day in Thüringen, so no shift under § 193 BGB is needed. This is a statutory deadline, not one printed in the letter, hence lower confidence.

warnings: The 12-month objection deadline (2027-11-18) is based on the general statutory rule of § 556 Abs. 3 BGB, not on a date printed in the letter itself; the landlord could in principle set a different (shorter, tenant-favourable) arrangement in the Mietvertrag, which was not provided.

The IBAN printed (DE49 8205 0084 0005 5840 00) is a well-formed German IBAN consistent with the sender's details, but ownership cannot be verified from the letter alone; confirm payee-name matching before paying if your bank flags a mismatch.
